comment: Declarative metadata for the per-interface config files, config/interface.<name>.
Same shape and same vocabulary as settings.json, so the network configuration UI can
eventually be generated from this the way the rest of the settings pages are.
Today two consumers read it, and they read one key:
"gatherStats": true  -- this field may leave the device.
www/api/controllers/stats.php includes those fields in the statistics payload, and
scripts/generate_crash_report includes them in a crash report. Everything else is
withheld. That is an ALLOWLIST on purpose: a field added here without gatherStats is
withheld automatically, whereas a denylist would have to be remembered every time.
It has been got wrong before -- an earlier denylist covered PSK and SSID but not
BACKUPPSK and BACKUPSSID. Both consumers also fail closed if this file is missing.
"type": "password" and "pii": true carry the same meaning as in settings.json and
mark why a field is withheld. They are documentation and belt-and-braces; the thing
that actually permits disclosure is gatherStats.
Fields are those written by network_set_interface() in www/api/controllers/network.php.

INTERFACE.name: INTERFACE
INTERFACE.tip: Kernel name of the interface, for example eth0 or wlan0.

PROTO.name: PROTO
PROTO.tip: Whether the interface takes its address from DHCP or uses a fixed one. A device on DHCP whose address changes while a show is running fails in ways that look nothing like a static misconfiguration, which is why this is the one addressing field included in reports.

ADDRESS.name: ADDRESS
ADDRESS.tip: Static IPv4 address for this interface.

NETMASK.name: NETMASK
NETMASK.tip: Subnet mask used with the static address.

GATEWAY.name: GATEWAY
GATEWAY.tip: Default gateway used with the static address.

SSID.name: SSID
SSID.tip: The name of a wireless network identifies a household on its own, so it is never included in statistics or crash reports.

HIDDEN.name: HIDDEN
HIDDEN.tip: The network does not broadcast its SSID.

WPA3.name: WPA3
WPA3.tip: Use WPA3 rather than WPA2 for this network.

IPFORWARDING.name: IPFORWARDING
IPFORWARDING.tip: Forward traffic between this interface and the others.

DHCPSERVER.name: DHCPSERVER
DHCPSERVER.tip: Hand out addresses on this interface.

DHCPPOOLSIZE.name: DHCPPOOLSIZE
DHCPPOOLSIZE.tip: How many addresses the DHCP server may hand out.

DHCPOFFSET.name: DHCPOFFSET
DHCPOFFSET.tip: First address in the DHCP pool, as an offset into the subnet.

ROUTEMETRIC.name: ROUTEMETRIC
ROUTEMETRIC.tip: Priority of this interface's default route; lower wins.
